\(R^2\) & r\_squared & Higher is better & Coefficient of determination. Higher values indicate that the fitted curve follows more of the observed response pattern. This remains an unweighted descriptive score when SD/SEM is supplied. \\
Adjusted \(R^2\) & adjusted\_r\_squared & Higher is better & \(R^2\) adjusted for the number of fitted parameters. It can decrease when extra parameters do not improve the fit enough to justify the added complexity. \\
MSE & mse & Lower is better & Average squared difference between observed and fitted values. Lower values indicate smaller model errors, but the squared units can be harder to interpret directly. \\
RMSE & rmse & Lower is better & Typical model error in the units of the fitted output on the analyzed scale. Lower values indicate predictions closer to the observations. This remains an unweighted descriptive score when SD/SEM is supplied. \\
MAE & mae & Lower is better & Average absolute model error in the units of the fitted output on the analyzed scale. Lower values indicate predictions closer to the observations. \\
NRMSE (mean) & mnrmse & Lower is better & RMSE divided by the mean of the observed analyzed outputs. Lower values indicate smaller relative error when the mean is positive and away from zero; near-zero or negative means make that interpretation unsuitable. \\
NRMSE (std. dev.) & nrmse & Lower is better & RMSE divided by the standard deviation of the observed analyzed outputs. Lower values indicate smaller error relative to the trajectory's variation, not relative to supplied observation SD/SEM. \\
AIC & aic & Lower is better & Akaike Information Criterion. AIC compares fitted models by considering both fit quality and the number of fitted parameters. Among comparable fitted models, a lower AIC value generally indicates better empirical support for a model that fits the data without unnecessary complexity. Absolute AIC values, including negative values, are not standalone quality grades. Supplied-error fits use a normal likelihood for the supplied observation-error model on the analyzed scale. \\
AIC\textsubscript{c} & aicc & Lower is better & Corrected Akaike Information Criterion. AIC\textsubscript{c} is AIC with an added small-sample correction that becomes increasingly relevant when the number of fitted observations is limited relative to the number of fitted parameters. The app retains its conventional correction when SD/SEM is supplied; it is an approximation rather than an exact small-sample guarantee for every fitted model. Among comparable fitted models, a lower AIC\textsubscript{c} value generally indicates better empirical support for a model that balances fit quality and complexity; AIC\textsubscript{c} is undefined when there are too few observations relative to the number of parameters. \\
BIC & bic & Lower is better & Bayesian Information Criterion. BIC compares fitted models by considering both fit quality and the number of fitted parameters, usually applying a stronger penalty for extra parameters than AIC. Among comparable fitted models, a lower BIC value generally indicates better empirical support for a model that fits the data without unnecessary complexity. Absolute BIC values, including negative values, are not standalone quality grades. Supplied-error fits use a normal likelihood for the supplied observation-error model on the analyzed scale. \\
